title: CI's Rust legs stall on headless Chrome: prez acceptance AT21 hung on macOS at 2.14.8's tag, and showreel AT23 and AT29 timed out at frame 0 on ubuntu at 1434e764
body:
## What

Twice in two days, one of CI's Rust legs stalled on the headless Chrome that prez's acceptance suites drive. On macOS, at 2.14.8's tag, prez acceptance AT21 hung with no output for more than 17 minutes, until the leg was cancelled and re-run. On ubuntu, on main's push of 1434e764, showreel AT23 and AT29 hit showreel's 30 s reply bound at frame 0 and turned main red. Before each stall, the same suites were green on code that matters to them: nothing between the two runs changes opt/prez or the Rust job.

Today a stall turns main red or holds the post-cut CI verdict until someone re-runs the leg. Once ST0011/10's reshape fires CI's macOS legs on candidate/ (devbin-vc's message of 31 Oct), the same stall would hold a release.

## Measured

Read 31 Oct 2026 by utilz-vc, from GitHub's jobs API and the job logs of tests.yml ("Utilz Tests"):

- 2.14.8's tag run 41127538028 at f2021ddc, attempt 1, "Rust (macos-latest)", step 10 "Build, test and accept every Rust crate". prez acceptance AT21 ("numbering: a deck default, a per-slide override, read off a real PDF", browser resolved to `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`) printed its second case's last check at 21:05:02Z. Nothing followed until "The operation was canceled." at 21:22:30Z. tests.yml sets no `timeout-minutes`, and no newer run shared its concurrency group, so neither a timeout nor a superseding run cancelled it. Attempt 2 re-ran the leg green in 11m07s, from 21:23:10Z to 21:34:17Z.
- main's push run 41140741047 at 1434e764, "Rust (ubuntu-latest)", step 10. prez showreel's black-box suite passed 14 and failed 2: AT23 and AT29 each failed with "showreel: no reply from Chrome in 30 s, during frame 0: screenshot". The step ended with "1 black-box suite failure(s) in opt/prez/crate.", and Test Summary went red with it. The macOS legs are skipped on a push.
- `git diff --stat f2021ddc..1434e764`, outside the whiteboard and the events, is `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (+6, the macOS job), `opt/menuz/test/macos.bats`, `intent/wip.md` and issue 0130's canon file. f2021ddc was green on main's push (41127529723) and on the tag's attempt 2.
- Of the last 40 runs of tests.yml, 35 succeeded, 3 were cancelled and 2 failed. The other failure, at 05538ca3 (run 41115734657), was "Test on Ubuntu"'s `setup_file`: a different job and a different cause.
- showreel's 30 s bound and its message are at `opt/prez/crate/crates/showreel/src/cdp.rs:206`. Its own tests are at cdp.rs:337 and :363, and `opt/prez/crate/test/video.sh:616` greps for the message.

## Design

dc, 31 Oct 2026, on devbin-vc's word (it holds hv's pen) and under utilz-vc's terms. Read from the code at ac2b8057 and from the two jobs' logs. Size S.

### What the logs add

- **AT21's stall is prez's own wait, and nothing bounds it.** On the macOS leg (job 124309847331, attempt 1), AT21's first two prints took 1.9 s and 1.8 s from start to "(rendered)": 21:04:57.90Z to 21:04:59.81Z, and 21:05:00.14Z to 21:05:01.93Z. The third, "deck on, slide 2 a title slide" (acceptance.sh:1474, through `renders` at :1460), never returned. `prez pdf` prints with `Command::output()` (drive.rs:50), which waits for Chrome to exit and for both of its pipes to close, with no deadline. A Chrome that never exits, or any process of Chrome's that keeps one of those pipes open, holds prez, the suite and the leg until something kills them. tests.yml sets no `timeout-minutes`, so GitHub's 360-minute default is the only other bound.
- **showreel's red is one stall, not two.** AT23 and AT29 share recording `two`, the paced run (video.sh:239-241), which `ensure` records once and keeps for every AT after it (video.sh:317). AT23's line reads "a recording failed:  / showreel: no reply ...". Recording `one`, unpaced, said nothing and passed, and AT24 to AT27 and AT30, which read it, passed. Chrome's own log stamps, on the runner's clock, which is UTC, put recording `two`'s load at 22:53:30.67. It was refused at 22:54:00.64Z, 30 s later, during frame 0: screenshot. showreel did what AC-02.6 asks: it bounded the wait (record.rs:41), named the step and printed Chrome's account (video.sh:344). That account ends with "Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU.": Chrome starting an on-device model, which none of showreel's flags turns off. That fits a first frame starved of CPU, but one log line does not prove it.
- Neither cause can be settled without repeated real runs, and the issue is low. So the fix makes each stall end soon and by name, then runs it once more, which is what both tools' remedy already tells a person to do: "run it again; if it fails at the same step twice, report the step".

### The change

1. **prez bounds its print** (drive.rs). Chrome writes its stdout and stderr to a file in the print's scratch directory rather than to pipes, so nothing Chrome leaves behind can hold prez on a pipe, and it stays in prez's own process group, so Ctrl-C at the terminal still reaches it (vc, 31 Oct, on critic-rust's high: a group of its own cut it off). prez waits for Chrome's main process for up to `PRINT_DEADLINE`, 120 s: sixty times the measured print, and well past the 5 s `--virtual-time-budget`. A print still running then is killed, while it is unreaped and its pid is still Chrome's, then reaped within a short grace, and the refusal says Chrome is "still running as pid N" if the grace runs out; no wait is unbounded. The refusal names the deadline and the PDF, with Chrome's captured output and the remedy "run it again; if it stalls twice, report it with Chrome's version". A helper Chrome leaves behind holds only the log. If prez cannot ask whether Chrome has finished, it says so with Chrome's output and that Chrome may still be running as pid N, unsignalled. The exit-status and no-PDF refusals keep their wording.
2. **A refused print never touches the PDF** (drive.rs; vc, 31 Oct, on critic-shell's medium). Chrome prints to `<out>.partial` beside `out`, any stale partial removed first. Only a print that exits 0 having written it is renamed over `out`, and then counted by `verify_pagination`. Every refusal removes the partial, and says so when it cannot. So a retry cannot pass on what a refused attempt left at `-o`, and prez's PDFs work as showreel's videos do: no partial ever looks finished. **The partial's name and its removal move to a new module, `artifact::partial`** (vc, 31 Oct, on Highlander: by the crate's own rule, lib.rs:3-6, the move and its second consumer land together, as `scratch` did for 0095's `pdf`). `remove_partial` (video.rs:596) keeps its name, its rule that a partial already gone counts as removed, its message and its test (video.rs:703-730). `partial_of` (video.rs:323) and the extension it is built from, `PARTIAL` (deliver.rs:499), go with it, keeping their names and `partial_of`'s test (video.rs:681-687), since prez's own would be their second copy. showreel's callers import them (video.rs:118, 218, 235, 247, 353, 371, 511, 555 and 565; deliver.rs:505, `is_partial`, which stays showreel's), and lib.rs gains the module's paragraph.
3. **The suites run a stalled command once more.** `renders` (lib/harness.sh:118) and `ensure` (video.sh:231) retry once when, and only when, the first attempt's refusal line is a stall: `stalled` matches `^(prez|showreel): ` and then prez's "did not finish printing" or showreel's "no reply from Chrome in". Each prints one RETRY line, worded once, and the first attempt's whole account before the retry, so the log still shows the stall, and a second stall fails with its own whole account, as the remedy says. Before its retry, `ensure` removes that recording's frames, its video, its TMPDIR and each `_out/` entry the stalled attempt added, and deletes nothing outside `_out/`; if any of that cannot be removed, the check fails rather than retry on top of what is left. showreel's message (cdp.rs:206) gains a comment that the suites key on its words.
4. **Offered, not in this change:** showreel turning off Chrome's on-device models (`--disable-features=OptimizationGuideModelDownloading,OptimizationHintsFetching,OptimizationTargetPrediction,OptimizationHints`, Puppeteer's set) as a fix for the frame-0 cause. It rests on one log line, and proving it needs AT23's determinism on real runs. vc, 31 Oct: not in; a lead if a stall recurs after this change.
5. The CI backstop, a `timeout-minutes` on the Rust job, goes in ST0031/02's bank, and CI proves it at the sweep's push.

Files: opt/prez/crate/src/drive.rs; opt/prez/crate/src/deck.rs (the log's path); opt/prez/crate/test/lib/harness.sh; opt/prez/crate/test/video.sh; a comment in opt/prez/crate/crates/showreel/src/cdp.rs; help/prez.md (a print's two minutes and its partial); opt/prez/crate/Cargo.toml and prez's entry in opt/prez/crate/Cargo.lock, taking prez from 2.5.9 to 2.5.10 as 0101 did, with artifact and showreel staying at 0.1.0; CHANGELOG.md, opening `## [2.14.9] - unreleased`, the next patch, whose number is hv's at the cut, with one `### Fixed` line for 0131 (vc, 31 Oct); opt/prez/crate/crates/artifact/src/partial.rs (new) and lib.rs (its paragraph); opt/prez/crate/crates/showreel/src/video.rs and deliver.rs (the moved items gone, their callers importing them). record.rs is untouched: showreel's `kill_group` stays where it is.

### Proof

Run at devbin-vc's desk on utilz-vc's GO of 31 Oct, in the worktree wt-0131 at v3's bytes (0131-v3.patch, sha256 5d25b2dc56158f5690366069bc3f2b4e4710fe8d9158fce0351b9547d6205506, on d567e4b8), with no CARGO_TARGET_DIR exported, through `run-0131.sh`, which refused any other bytes. v3 landed as 5d83dd93, on 21cf748f, whose change (`git diff --binary 21cf748f 5d83dd93`) hashes to the bank's sha256, 13 files, +682/-170 (checked by utilz-vc).

- **R1, slot 01M68X3J16EWFB34DVFE9J4MHR (cargo lane), 11:58:03Z to 11:58:36Z, green.** `cargo test --workspace` exited 0, its counts as printed: artifact `ok. 44 passed; 0 failed`, prez `ok. 171 passed; 0 failed`, tests/manifest.rs `ok. 5 passed; 0 failed`, showreel `ok. 199 passed; 0 failed`, and the showreel binary and both doc-test runs `ok. 0 passed; 0 failed`, with 0 ignored in any. The new tests are each ok: (a) `a_print_that_never_finishes_is_refused_at_its_deadline_and_chrome_killed`, refused at a 3 s deadline, killed and reaped within the grace, the 30 s sleep it orphaned killed by the test; (b) `a_print_returns_when_chrome_exits_whatever_it_leaves_holding_its_output`, over a stale partial; (c) `a_print_that_fails_is_refused_with_what_chrome_said`; (d) `a_print_refused_after_writing_its_pdf_leaves_no_pdf_and_no_partial`; and (e) `a_stale_partial_is_never_taken_for_a_print_that_wrote_nothing`, which seeds a whole one-page partial under a fake that exits 0 having written nothing, and goes red without the stale partial's removal (utilz-vc's red-control). The two tests that moved with `remove_partial` and `partial_of` are ok in artifact: `partial::tests::a_partial_is_the_video_s_name_and_more` and `partial::tests::a_partial_that_cannot_be_removed_is_named_issue_0096`. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings` each exited 0. Log: ~/Devel/scratch/utilz-dc/r1-0131-v3.log, 610 lines, sha256 a224cf7002abbfbe.
- **R2, slot 01M68X84Z53D8CCYNM0K0T0B76 (heavy lane), 11:59:50Z to 12:00:38Z, green.** acceptance.sh printed `AT21: PASS` on its four decks, printed by rhadamanth's Chrome through the partial with every page number as wanted, then `passed 1   failed 0   skipped 0   n/a 0`. video.sh printed `AT23: PASS`, 150 frames in each recording, the paced one paused 229 times, 0 frames differing, and `AT29: PASS`, then `passed 2   failed 0   skipped 0`. No RETRY line printed. Log: ~/Devel/scratch/utilz-dc/r2-0131-v3.log, 59 lines, sha256 d012dd010c75c4e7.
- (a) and (b) would be red on the old `output()` path, which reading shows: it had no deadline to inject and waited for the pipes. The retry branches are proven by reading: a stub for a suite would be a test of the test. A residual risk of written fakes, named and not guarded (vc, 31 Oct): on Linux, an exec can race a fork in another test thread while the script is still open for writing there, and fail with ETXTBSY, "Text file busy". That reads as itself, not as this change.
- CI's proof on runners comes with hv's dispatch or the next push of main.
